note: Demand list for the facts phase. Hypotheses come from memory and research notes (FREQUENCY, FRESHNESS, STARTUP); they are questions to check, never evidence. Lens names: numbers | behavior | decisions+changes | faq. look_in entries are full snapshot source ids. Facts owned by other chapters are listed under link_existing: link them, do not duplicate. Fact namespaces: cloudfront (ids cloudfront-...) and global-accelerator (ids global-accelerator-...).

demand.question: How many distributions can one AWS account create by default, and can the quota be raised?
demand.hypothesis: 200 per account, adjustable
demand.note: Quota page: 500 distributions per AWS account, adjustable (hypothesis 200 is outdated). Looked in cloudfront-limits table 1 and the FAQ (the FAQ points to the quotas page). adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: How many cache behaviors, origins and origin groups can one distribution have?
demand.hypothesis: 25 cache behaviors, 25 origins, 10 origin groups (adjustable)
demand.note: Quota page: 75 cache behaviors, 100 origins, 10 origin groups per distribution, all adjustable. Hypothesis (25 / 25 / 10) is outdated except origin groups. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What is the maximum size of one file (one response) that CloudFront delivers?
demand.hypothesis: 30 GB per HTTP GET response (older material says 20 GB)
demand.note: Two statements disagree: quotas page says maximum cacheable file size per HTTP GET response is 50 GB (request body 64 GB); the FAQ (older text) says 30 GB for a single file. Both recorded; adjudicator should keep both with scope or prefer the quotas page. register-15: teach 50 GB cacheable per GET response (cloudfront-quota-max-cacheable-file-size); the FAQ 30 GB fact is reference only adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; removed rejected cloudfront-faq-max-single-file-30-gb.

demand.question: What are the per-distribution quotas on requests per second and data transfer rate, and what does the FAQ say for peaks above 150 Gbps or 250,000 RPS?
demand.hypothesis: 250,000 RPS and 150 Gbps per distribution, adjustable; contact AWS for higher peaks
demand.note: 150 Gbps and 250,000 requests per second per distribution, adjustable, not applied to flat-rate plans. FAQ: request higher limits, capacity added within two business days. Hypothesis confirmed. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: How many alternate domain names (CNAMEs) can one distribution have?
demand.hypothesis: 100, adjustable
demand.note: 100 alternate domain names per distribution, adjustable. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What are the default and allowed values of the origin response timeout, origin keep-alive timeout, connection attempts and connection timeout?
demand.hypothesis: response timeout 30 s default (1 to 120, more by quota); keep-alive 5 s default (1 to 120); 3 attempts; 10 s connection timeout
demand.note: Response timeout 1-120 s (default 30), connection attempts 1-3 (default 3), connection timeout 1-10 s (default 10), keep-alive default 5 s confirmed. Keep-alive range is 1-300 s on the quotas page (hypothesis said 1-120). Origin ports: 80, 443, 1024-65535, defaults 80 and 443. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; close-facts-15: verified in the second vote round:cloudfront-default-connect-wait-before-failover.

demand.question: What are the default values of minimum TTL, default TTL and maximum TTL, and how do Cache-Control max-age and s-maxage interact with them?
demand.hypothesis: minimum 0 s, default 86,400 s (24 hours), maximum 31,536,000 s (one year); headers win between min and max
demand.note: Default TTL 86400 s (one day), Maximum TTL 31536000 s (one year). The saved pages do not state a default Minimum TTL of 0; 0 appears only in managed cache policy settings (using-managed-cache-policies), not as a default. The max-age and s-maxage interplay is in the table of Expiration (mined by the behavior lens). adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: How many invalidation paths are free each month, how is a wildcard path counted, and how many file and wildcard invalidations can be in progress at one time?
demand.hypothesis: first 1,000 paths a month free per account; a wildcard path counts as one path; 3,000 file paths or 15 wildcard paths in progress
demand.note: First 1,000 paths a month free and wildcard counts as one path confirmed. In-progress limits (3,000 objects, 15 wildcard paths) are only in the FAQ; the current quotas page lists 150 paths or tags per second and 1 wildcard invalidation per second instead. Both recorded. Price after the free paths: $0.005 per path. register-15: teach the quotas-page rates; the FAQ in-progress figures (3,000 objects, 15 wildcard paths) are reference only adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; removed rejected cloudfront-faq-invalidation-individual-objects-in-progress.

demand.question: For how long does CloudFront cache an error response from the origin by default (error caching minimum TTL)?
demand.hypothesis: 10 seconds by default
demand.note: Default error caching minimum TTL is 10 seconds (georestrictions page; DownloadDistValuesErrorPages states no number). adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: How many key groups per distribution and public keys per key group are allowed for signed URLs and signed cookies?
demand.hypothesis: 4 key groups per cache behavior, 5 public keys per key group
demand.note: 4 key groups per cache behavior, 5 public keys per key group, 10 key groups per account; all adjustable. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What are the limits of CloudFront Functions: maximum function size, memory, execution time model, and functions per account?
demand.hypothesis: 10 KB code, 2 MB memory, sub-millisecond execution; 100 functions per account
demand.note: 10 KB code (not adjustable), 2 MB memory, 100 functions per account, submillisecond duration. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What are the Lambda@Edge limits for viewer events versus origin events: timeout, memory, package size and response size?
demand.hypothesis: viewer events 5 s and 128 MB, 1 MB package; origin events 30 s and up to 10,240 MB, 50 MB package
demand.note: Current pages: Lambda@Edge timeout 30 s for all four event types, memory 128 MB for viewer events and 10,240 MB for origin events, code 50 MB for both, generated response 40 KB (viewer) and 1 MB (origin). Hypothesis (viewer 5 s, 1 MB package) is outdated. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; removed rejected cloudfront-quota-lambda-edge-requests-per-second.

demand.question: How large can a CloudFront KeyValueStore be, and what are the key and value size limits?
demand.hypothesis: 5 MB per store; key 512 bytes; value 1 KB
demand.note: 5 MB per store, key 512 Bytes, value 1 KB. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: How many headers, cookies and query strings can a cache policy or origin request policy name, and how many custom policies per account?
demand.hypothesis: 10 each per policy; 20 cache policies per account
demand.note: 10 each per cache policy and per origin request policy (all adjustable), 20 custom cache policies per account. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What quotas apply to SSL/TLS certificates with CloudFront: custom certificates per account, dedicated-IP certificates per account, certificates per distribution?
demand.hypothesis: one certificate per distribution; dedicated IP certificates 2 per account by default; certificates per account adjustable
demand.note: 1 certificate per distribution; 2 dedicated-IP SSL certificates per account by default, adjustable, no quota with SNI. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: Which certificate key types and maximum RSA key sizes does CloudFront accept for viewer certificates, and what key size for ACM certificates?
demand.hypothesis: RSA 1024, 2048, 3072, 4096 bits; ECDSA 256 and 384; ACM RSA 2048
demand.note: RSA 1024/2048/3072/4096 bits, max 4096; ECDSA 256 and 384; ACM issues RSA up to 2048 bits. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; close-facts-15: verified in the second vote round:cloudfront-cert-ecdsa-key-sizes-supported.

demand.question: How many fields can a field-level encryption profile encrypt, and what other field-level encryption quotas exist (request body size)?
demand.hypothesis: up to 10 data fields; profiles per account; maximum length of a field
demand.note: 10 fields per profile, 10 fields in a request body, request body 1 MB, field 16 KB, 10 profiles and 10 configurations per account. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: How many IP addresses does a CloudFront Anycast static IP list provide, and what price class does it require?
demand.hypothesis: 21 IPv4 addresses; price class All (use all edge locations)
demand.note: 21 addresses for allow-listing, 3 for apex domains (the dual-stack counts are in the FAQ facts); requires price class All (Use all edge locations). adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What sampling rate range do real-time logs accept, where are they delivered, and how fast are they delivered?
demand.hypothesis: sampling 1 to 100 percent; Kinesis Data Streams; within seconds
demand.note: Sampling rate: whole number 1 to 100; delivered to Kinesis Data Streams within seconds, best effort. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: Which destinations do standard logs (v2) support, are standard logs free, and how quickly are log files delivered?
demand.hypothesis: Amazon S3, CloudWatch Logs, Amazon Data Firehose; standard logs free (destination charges apply); delivered within minutes to an hour (best effort)
demand.note: Destinations and no extra charge for enabling standard logs are in facts of other lenses. NOT FOUND: how quickly standard log files are delivered; AccessLogs, standard-logging and the FAQ give no delivery time for v2 logs. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What are the price classes, which is the default, and what do they trade off?
demand.hypothesis: All edge locations (default), Price Class 200, Price Class 100; cheaper classes exclude the most expensive Regions, higher latency for some viewers
demand.note: Price Class All (default), 200, 100 from the pay-as-you-go price class table. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What are the pay-as-you-go pricing dimensions of CloudFront (data transfer out, requests, invalidation paths, real-time logs, functions, Origin Shield, dedicated IP SSL, field-level encryption), and is data transfer from AWS origins to CloudFront charged?
demand.hypothesis: billed for data transfer out to the internet and HTTP/HTTPS requests by Region; origin fetch from AWS origins free; dedicated IP custom SSL has a monthly fee
demand.note: Dimensions and unit prices from the pay-as-you-go page. NOT FOUND in a quotable line: the unit of request pricing (per 10,000 requests appears only in a heading), so the HTTP and HTTPS request prices were rejected by M5 and not stored. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What does the CloudFront always-free tier include each month (data transfer out, requests, CloudFront Functions invocations)?
demand.hypothesis: 1 TB data out, 10 million HTTP/HTTPS requests, 2 million CloudFront Functions invocations each month
demand.note: 1 TB data transfer out, 10,000,000 requests, 2,000,000 CloudFront Functions invocations a month (FAQ sentence). Mined mainly by another lens. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What are the CloudFront flat-rate plans (Free, Pro, Business, Premium): monthly price per distribution, request and data allowances, overage charges, and what they include?
demand.hypothesis: $0, $15, $200, $1,000 per month per distribution; no overage charges; include WAF, DDoS protection, Route 53 DNS, TLS certificate, S3 credits (volatile; GA 2025-11-18)
demand.note: $0, $15, $200, $1,000 a month per distribution, no overage charges; allowances 1M/10M/125M/500M requests. Volatile. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What monthly uptime percentage does the CloudFront SLA commit to?
demand.hypothesis: 99.9 percent
demand.note: At least 99.9% monthly uptime; credits 10%, 25%, 100%. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; close-facts-15: verified in the second vote round:cloudfront-sla-credit-10-percent, cloudfront-sla-credit-100-percent.

demand.question: Which objects does CloudFront compress automatically: file size range, compression formats, and what the request must include?
demand.hypothesis: 1,000 to 10,000,000 bytes; Gzip and Brotli; Accept-Encoding header; Content-Length present
demand.note: 1,000 to 10,000,000 bytes; status 200, 403 or 404; Accept-Encoding with gzip or br; Content-Length required. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What are the Global Accelerator quotas: accelerators per account, listeners per accelerator, port ranges per listener, endpoint groups per listener, endpoints per endpoint group?
demand.hypothesis: 20 accelerators; 10 listeners; 10 port ranges; one endpoint group per Region; 10 endpoints per endpoint group
demand.note: 20 standard accelerators, 10 listeners, 10 port ranges, 42 endpoint groups per accelerator, 10 endpoints per endpoint group; one endpoint group per Region per listener. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: How many static IP addresses does a standard accelerator get for IPv4 and for dual-stack, and how long do they stay assigned?
demand.hypothesis: two static IPv4 addresses; dual-stack two IPv4 and two IPv6; kept while the accelerator exists, even when disabled; lost on delete
demand.note: Two static IPv4; dual-stack four (two IPv4, two IPv6); kept while the accelerator exists, even when disabled; lost on delete. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication. close-facts-15: global-accelerator-dec-static-ips-deleted-with-accelerator was rejected; keep and delete behavior rests on global-accelerator-static-ips-kept-until-delete; status stays filled.

demand.question: What range and default does a Global Accelerator traffic dial have?
demand.hypothesis: 0 to 100 percent; default 100
demand.note: Range 0 to 100, default 100 (CreateEndpointGroup API reference). adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; removed rejected global-accelerator-traffic-dial-range-0-to-100, global-accelerator-traffic-dial-api-default-100. Default 100% is verified in the FAQ fact and setting the dial to 0 in the guide fact; the 0 to 100 range is not found as a quotable sentence (do not state it).

demand.question: What range and default does a Global Accelerator endpoint weight have?
demand.hypothesis: 0 to 255; default 128
demand.note: Range 0 to 255, default 128. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; close-facts-15: verified in the second vote round:global-accelerator-endpoint-weight-range-0-to-255.

demand.question: What are the Global Accelerator health check settings (interval choices, threshold count) for EC2 and Elastic IP endpoints?
demand.hypothesis: interval 10 or 30 seconds (default 30); threshold count 3
demand.note: Interval 10 or 30 s (default 30); threshold count default 3 (range 1-10). Source is the CreateEndpointGroup API reference (fetched by this agent); the developer guide pages give no numbers. Options apply to EC2 and Elastic IP endpoints only. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: How fast does Global Accelerator fail over between Regions, and why is it faster than DNS-based failover?
demand.hypothesis: within seconds (FAQ: 'in less than 1 minute' or similar); no dependence on DNS TTL or client caching
demand.note: FAQ: unhealthy endpoint detected and taken out of service in less than one minute. Recovery to regular routing about 30 seconds. The DNS comparison is in facts of the decisions lens. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; close-facts-15: verified in the second vote round:global-accelerator-recovery-routing-about-30-seconds.

demand.question: What are the Global Accelerator pricing dimensions: fixed hourly fee per accelerator, Data Transfer-Premium in the dominant direction, public IPv4 charges?
demand.hypothesis: $0.025 per hour per accelerator (enabled or disabled); DT-Premium per GB in the dominant direction, on top of EC2 data transfer out
demand.note: $0.025 per hour per accelerator, enabled or disabled; DT-Premium in the dominant direction, on top of EC2 data transfer out; public IPv4 charges. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What idle timeouts does Global Accelerator apply to TCP and UDP flows?
demand.hypothesis: TCP 340 seconds; UDP 30 seconds
demand.note: TCP 340 s, UDP 30 s, not customizable. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: How many destinations can a custom routing accelerator address, and which endpoints does it support?
demand.hypothesis: VPC subnet endpoints only (EC2 instances); up to 64,000 destinations per ... with ways to go beyond
demand.note: VPC subnet endpoints with EC2 instances only; subnet /28 to /17. NOT FOUND: the figure 64,000 destinations appears only inside an FAQ question heading, not in an answer or a quotable sentence. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What is the most specific prefix and how many address ranges can be brought to Global Accelerator with BYOIP?
demand.hypothesis: /24 IPv4; up to 2 ranges per account
demand.note: At most two ranges, most specific prefix /24 (FAQ facts by another lens). adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What monthly uptime percentage does the Global Accelerator SLA commit to?
demand.hypothesis: 99.99 percent
demand.note: There are two commitments: Multi-AZ accelerators (credit tiers start below 99.99%) and Single-AZ accelerators (credit tiers start below 99.5%). The SLA page states the thresholds in tables, not as one sentence. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; close-facts-15: verified in the second vote round:global-accelerator-sla-multi-az-credit-10-percent.

demand.question: How many CloudFront points of presence, regional edge caches and countries/cities does AWS state today, and how many Global Accelerator edge locations?
demand.hypothesis: 600+ POPs and 13 regional edge caches (volatile); state as 'AWS states, as of <date>'
demand.note: GA: 130 Points of Presence in 95 cities across 53 countries (features page). CloudFront: only '750+ global edge locations' in the flat-rate plan table. NOT FOUND: 600+ POPs and 13 regional edge caches; the saved CloudFront features, FAQ and Introduction pages list locations but give no totals. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What expiration and validity options does a signed URL have with a canned policy versus a custom policy (start time, IP range, wildcards), and which hash algorithms are supported?
demand.hypothesis: canned: expiry only, one file; custom: start date, end date, IP range, wildcard in resource; SHA-1 and SHA-256 (2026-04-01)
demand.note: Canned: expiry only, no start time, no IP range, no reuse; custom: optional start time and IP range, reusable with wildcards. Hash-Algorithm values SHA1 and SHA256, default SHA1 on the current pages; the 2026-04-01 SHA-256 What's New item belongs to the changes lens. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; close-facts-15: verified in the second vote round:cloudfront-signed-url-hash-algorithm-default-sha1.

demand.question: How long is the WebSocket connection allowed through CloudFront, and is there a WebSocket quota?
demand.hypothesis: quota table 12 'Quotas on WebSocket connections'
demand.note: Quota table 12: origin response timeout (idle timeout) for WebSocket is 10 minutes. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What is CloudFront, in AWS's own words, and how does a request reach the edge location that serves it (lowest latency)?
demand.hypothesis: web service that speeds up distribution of static and dynamic content through a worldwide network of edge locations; DNS routes the request to the POP with the lowest latency
demand.note: adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What do regional edge caches do, which requests skip them (proxy methods, dynamic requests, same-Region S3), and are they enabled by default?
demand.hypothesis: mid-tier cache between POPs and origin; PUT/POST/PATCH/OPTIONS/DELETE and dynamic requests go directly to origin; S3 in same Region skips the REC; enabled by default, no extra charge
demand.note: adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: Which origin types can a distribution use (S3 bucket, S3 website endpoint as custom origin, MediaStore and MediaPackage, ALB, NLB, EC2, Lambda function URL, API Gateway, any HTTP server outside AWS)?
demand.hypothesis: all of these; non-AWS origins allowed
demand.note: adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; close-facts-15: verified in the second vote round:cloudfront-faq-content-types-http-websocket.

demand.question: How do cache behaviors with path patterns route requests to different origins, in what order are they evaluated, and what is the default cache behavior?
demand.hypothesis: path patterns such as /images/*.jpg; evaluated in the listed order; default (*) behavior always last and cannot be deleted
demand.note: adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What viewer protocol policy options exist (HTTP and HTTPS, Redirect HTTP to HTTPS, HTTPS only) and what does each do?
demand.hypothesis: redirect returns 301 to HTTPS; HTTPS only returns 403 for HTTP
demand.note: Redirect returns 301 for GET/HEAD and 307 for other methods on HTTP 1.1 or above (using-https-viewers-to-cloudfront). The S3-origin page (using-https-cloudfront-to-s3-origin) says other methods get 403 under Redirect HTTP to HTTPS; the two pages differ and both are recorded in their scope. HTTPS Only returns 403. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What origin protocol policy options exist (HTTP only, HTTPS only, Match viewer), and can CloudFront use HTTPS to an S3 website endpoint origin?
demand.hypothesis: S3 website endpoints do not support HTTPS, so CloudFront uses HTTP to them; S3 REST endpoint supports HTTPS
demand.note: adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: Which certificate requirements apply to an alternate domain name on CloudFront: the ACM certificate Region, the certificate must cover the domain name, the default *.cloudfront.net certificate?

demand.hypothesis: SNI no extra charge, works with modern clients; dedicated IP serves legacy clients that lack SNI, monthly charge
demand.note: adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What does the viewer security policy control (minimum TLS version and ciphers), which policy is recommended, and which protocols (TLS 1.3, HTTP/2, HTTP/3) are supported?
demand.hypothesis: TLSv1.2_2021 recommended; TLS 1.3 supported; HTTP/3 over QUIC opt-in
demand.note: Partly filled: security policy meaning, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 needs, HTTP/3 needs TLSv1.3. NOT FOUND in the saved pages: a statement that TLSv1.2_2021 is the recommended security policy (looked in secure-connections-supported-viewer-protocols-ciphers, DownloadDistValuesGeneral, www/cloudfront/faqs). demand.question: How do you get end-to-end HTTPS (viewer to CloudFront and CloudFront to custom origin), and what must the origin certificate be (trusted CA, matching domain, not self-signed)?
demand.hypothesis: origin certificate must be signed by a trusted CA; self-signed certificates fail; domain must match origin domain or Host header
demand.note: adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication.

demand.question: What does field-level encryption do (encrypts selected POST fields at the edge with a public key so only the application with the private key can read them)?
demand.hypothesis: adds a layer on top of HTTPS; sensitive data stays encrypted through the application stack
demand.note: adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; close-facts-15: verified in the second vote round:cloudfront-fle-layer-on-https-selected-fields.

demand.question: What are viewer mutual TLS and origin mutual TLS on CloudFront, and when would you use them?
demand.hypothesis: viewer mTLS verifies client certificates against a trust store (2025-11-24); origin mTLS presents a client certificate to the origin (2026-02-02)
demand.note: Viewer mTLS (modes, edge validation) and origin mTLS (FAQ) filled. The guide page for origin mTLS is not in the corpus; the dates 2025-11-24 and 2026-02-02 belong to the changes lens. The FAQ says a trust store is mandatory for viewer mTLS while the guide says passthrough mode needs none; only the guide wording was mined. adjudicate-15: status set after adjudication; close-facts-15: verified in the second vote round:cloudfront-faq-origin-mtls-per-distribution-or-origin.

demand.question: What is origin access control (OAC), how does the S3 bucket policy allow it (service principal cloudfront.amazonaws.com with an AWS:SourceArn condition on the distribution), and why does the bucket stay private?

demand.note: OAC, bucket policy service principal cloudfront.amazonaws.com, Condition on the distribution, HTTPS when signing, signing behaviors filled. demand.question: How do you make a public ALB accept only CloudFront traffic (origin-facing managed prefix list in the security group plus a secret custom header checked by a listener rule)?
